words.sense: compensation or action making amends for harm caused
misconceptions: Every effort to make amends must return an identifiable item

words.sense: return or equivalent repayment of what was wrongfully taken
misconceptions: An apology or general payment for distress always returns a specific loss

semantic_axes.description: Making amends for wider harm differs from returning what someone wrongfully took.

edges.boundary_rule: reparation compensates for harm done; restitution returns what was wrongfully taken or its equivalent.
clues_a: public steps to repair wrongful harm
clues_b: equivalent value of taken property repaid

misconceptions.M1: All compensation is returning a stolen possession
misconceptions.M2: Returning stolen property necessarily compensates every kind of injury
misconceptions.M3: The publicity or emotional response determines the kind of remedy

chains.frame: Which word best describes Ayla's action after the theft?

beats.text: Ayla returned the calculator she had taken from her classmate's locker without permission.
beats.decisive_clue: exact object taken was returned to its owner
beats.reason: The purpose is to restore possession of a specific item.

beats.text: She also returned its original case, which she had kept with it.
beats.decisive_clue: remaining taken property was also restored
beats.reason: The remedy continues to replace what belonged to someone else.

chains.feedback_short: The decisive evidence remains remaining taken property was also restored.
chains.feedback_deep: Reparation means payment or action intended to repair injury or wrongdoing; restitution means restoring property or money to its rightful owner. The purpose is to restore possession of a specific item. The remedy continues to replace what belonged to someone else.
chains.contrast_rule: reparation compensates for harm done; restitution returns what was wrongfully taken or its equivalent.

hints.attention: Check what was taken and what was given back.
hints.axis: Making amends for wider harm differs from returning what someone wrongfully took.
hints.contrast: reparation compensates for harm done; restitution returns what was wrongfully taken or its equivalent.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Bilal's payment to his neighbour?

beats.text: After damaging his neighbour's fence with a football, Bilal paid for the broken boards and the repair work.
beats.decisive_clue: payment made amends for damage inflicted
beats.reason: He compensates harm rather than returning an item he stole.

beats.text: He also helped repaint the repaired section so the fence matched.
beats.decisive_clue: additional work repaired the damage done
beats.reason: The effort addresses resulting harm, not wrongful possession.

chains.feedback_short: The decisive evidence remains additional work repaired the damage done.
chains.feedback_deep: Reparation means payment or action intended to repair injury or wrongdoing; restitution means restoring property or money to its rightful owner. He compensates harm rather than returning an item he stole. The effort addresses resulting harm, not wrongful possession.
chains.contrast_rule: reparation compensates for harm done; restitution returns what was wrongfully taken or its equivalent.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Chloe's payment to her cousin?

beats.text: Chloe repaid the exact amount of savings she had taken from her cousin's wallet without permission.
beats.decisive_clue: specific wrongfully taken amount was paid back
beats.reason: The money is restored to its owner.

beats.text: She handed it back in a purple envelope.
beats.decisive_clue: return of taken money regardless of envelope
beats.reason: Packaging does not turn replacement of a particular loss into a broader remedy.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Gina's response after taking the headphones?

beats.text: Gina bought identical headphones to replace a pair she had taken and then lost from her roommate.
beats.decisive_clue: provided an equivalent for wrongfully taken property
beats.reason: Replacement restores the particular material loss.

beats.text: The new pair arrived in a bright yellow box.
beats.decisive_clue: equivalent property restored regardless of packaging
beats.reason: Box colour has no relation to the nature of the remedy.

chains.feedback_short: The distraction does not matter: equivalent property restored regardless of packaging.
chains.feedback_deep: Reparation means payment or action intended to repair injury or wrongdoing; restitution means restoring property or money to its rightful owner. Replacement restores the particular material loss. Box colour has no relation to the nature of the remedy.
chains.contrast_rule: reparation compensates for harm done; restitution returns what was wrongfully taken or its equivalent.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Hana's effort after defacing a mural?

beats.text: Hana paid to clean the mural she had painted over and funded materials to restore the damaged artwork.
beats.decisive_clue: paid to remedy physical harm she caused
beats.reason: The action repairs damage, not a taking of another's possession.

beats.text: The receipt listed paint removal, replacement supplies and the artists' hours repairing the same wall.
beats.decisive_clue: costs addressed damage rather than stolen property
beats.reason: The clarification identifies compensation for harm.
